lotteries.justification: Opening-magnitude risk. C is a certain smooth partial open held to the end (return 7.99, final openness 0.80, never reaches the target). Good branch A fully opens the drawer (return 9.79); bad branch B barely moves it (return 0.36, final 0.05). Reward indifference is p* = (7.99-0.36)/(9.79-0.36) = 0.809; p=0.79 sits just below it so the lottery's expected return (~7.81) is a shade under C (7.99), giving the reward a small-but-real preference for the certain partial open. A human who values actually getting the drawer fully open might take the 79% gamble instead.

lotteries.justification: Let-go reliability risk, a different shape from lottery 1 (different C, A, and B). C is a certain solid open held on the handle to the end (return 8.50). Good branch A opens slightly fuller and holds (return 9.70); bad branch B opens then withdraws and lets the drawer creep back (return 6.72). Reward indifference is p* = (8.50-6.72)/(9.70-6.72) = 0.597; p=0.58 is just below it, so expected lottery return (~8.45) is a touch under C (8.50) and the reward mildly prefers the sure thing. A human comfortable with the small creep-back risk might prefer the gamble.
